node.title: Re: Defining your own regex character class
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
There is an experimental feature (that I haven't used yet), [doc://perlrecharclass#Extended-Bracketed-Character-Classes], that should allow you to define your own classes (or more specifically, compose a character class out of others, which you can also interpolate into a regex).

However, /\b(?:[[:digit:]]{1,3}\.){3}[[:digit:]]{1,3}\b/ is not a character class (emphasis mine):

A character class is a way of denoting a set of characters in such a way that one character of the set is matched. It's important to remember that: matching a character class consumes exactly one character in the source string.

What you've got is a whole regex, and I think that [LanX] [id://1205771|is right] that simply compiling that into a variable with [doc://perlop#Regexp-Quote-Like-Operators|qr] and interpolating that into another regex is the best way to go. Later in that thread you asked if you could isolate the variable, and the usual [doc://perldata#Scalar-value-constructors|${}] can be applied here too, as well as the /x [doc://perlre#Modifiers|modifier]:

my $x = qr/foo/; my $y = qr/${x}bar/; # (?^:(?^:foo)bar) my $z = qr/ $x bar /x; # (?^x: (?^:foo) bar )

Regarding the example you've shown, note there is $RE{net}{IPv4} from [mod://Regexp::Common::net].

Minor edits for clarification.
